fixes.explanation: Lamps going out come up in another one of Jesus' teachings (Matthew 25:8), but not in this one. Here He warns, “Otherwise, he may arrive without notice and find you sleeping.” Sleeping is the warning in this verse, not lamps.
That's what Jesus says, friend: after that tribulation, the sun will be darkened. He says it plainly, so there's nothing to decode. Sit with that for a second, because Jesus doesn't rush it.
Standing still sounds dramatic, I'll give you that. But that's not what Jesus says. He says the sun will be darkened.
Hotter is a fair guess, since my oven turns up the heat when I want a bigger sizzle. But Jesus says nothing about the sun's heat in this verse. He says the sun will be darkened.
Yes. Jesus says the stars will fall from the sky. I read that line twice, because Jesus says it and I take it seriously.
Close, but Jesus does say it. In His words, the stars will fall from the sky. It's right there in verse 25, right after the verse about the sun and the moon.
Standing guard would make them sound steady and calm. But Jesus says the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Shaken is the word in this verse, not guard.
I get the thought, because Elijah, the prophet (1 Kings 17:1), is a big name. But look at what Jesus says. They will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds. Elijah isn't in this verse at all.

That's right, friend. In all that dark, Jesus says they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds. He doesn't mention Elijah anywhere in this passage. The Son of Man is Jesus' name for Himself (Mark 2:10).
A horse makes a grand picture, doesn't it? But Jesus doesn't mention a horse here. He says the Son of Man comes in the clouds with great power and glory.

GATHER. That's the word, baker! Jesus says He will send out the angels to gather His elect. The verse names the errand, and the errand is gathering. I'd sing about it if my mustache could carry a tune.

Judge is a big word in Bible talk, so I see why it jumped out. But Jesus says He will send out the angels to gather His elect. Judge isn't the word in this verse. Gather is, and I'd bet a whole batch on it.
Israel is a natural guess. But Jesus doesn't name any one land. He says from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven. The reach is much wider than one country.

Jerusalem is a well-known city, so I get the guess. But Jesus doesn't mention it in this verse. The angels gather from the four winds, from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven. That's way bigger than one city.

A rebuilt temple is a natural thing to guess, so I see the link. But Jesus says nothing about it being rebuilt in these verses. He says that when they see these things happening, they should know that He is near, right at the door.

True. Jesus says it Himself: no one knows about that day or hour, not even the angels in heaven, nor the Son, but only the Father. The angels are right there in heaven, and even they don't know. That's why I don't guess the day, I just keep my ovens ready.
That's it. The man puts each servant in charge of his own task. Each servant has something of his own to do.
Silver shows up in another one of Jesus' teachings (Matthew 25:18), but not in this picture. Here the man puts each servant in charge of his own task. It's about a task, not money.

A key makes sense for a house. I shared a junk drawer with a mystery key that kept guessing which door it opened. But Jesus doesn't mention a key in this picture. The man puts each servant in charge of his own task.

I can see why you'd think that, since Peter, James, John and Andrew were the ones who asked Him privately on the Mount of Olives (Mark 13:3). But Jesus widens it at the end. He says, “…what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!” The call reaches past those four.

Right, friend. Jesus says, “…what I say to you, I say to everyone: Keep watch!” It starts with the four who asked Him privately (Mark 13:3), but it doesn't stop there. The call to keep watch is for everyone, and that includes you.
